differences.title: 1. DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
differences.leftDesc: EVM is tailored for smart contract execution on Ethereum, focusing on gas metering and deterministic state changes for secure, trustless transactions.
differences.rightDesc: WASM is a portable, low-level bytecode format designed for efficient execution in browsers and on servers, providing a compilation target for multiple languages.

differences.title: 2. EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT
differences.leftDesc: EVM operates within a secure sandbox, managing its own state and preventing interference with the host system or other contracts.
differences.rightDesc: WASM runs in a sandboxed environment, enabling safe execution of untrusted code by restricting access to system resources.

differences.title: 3. GAS MECHANISM
differences.leftDesc: Every EVM operation consumes 'gas', which must be paid for in ETH, preventing infinite loops and resource abuse on the network.
differences.rightDesc: WASM execution doesn't inherently have a gas concept; resource limits are managed by the host environment or runtime.

differences.title: 4. LANGUAGE SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: EVM primarily executes bytecode compiled from Solidity, Vyper, and other Ethereum-specific smart contract languages.
differences.rightDesc: WASM is a compilation target for C, C++, Rust, Go, and many others, offering broad language interoperability.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: EVM's interpreter design and gas accounting prioritize security and determinism over raw execution speed, making it relatively slower.
differences.rightDesc: WASM's near-native speed is achieved through ahead-of-time (AOT) or just-in-time (JIT) compilation, offering significantly higher performance.

differences.title: 6. INTEROPERABILITY
differences.leftDesc: EVM is tightly coupled with the Ethereum ecosystem, interacting with other smart contracts and the blockchain state.
differences.rightDesc: WASM is designed for universal execution across web browsers, servers, IoT devices, and even other blockchains (e.g., Polkadot, NEAR).

differences.title: 7. EVOLUTION & USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: EVM's primary role is executing decentralized applications (dApps) and managing state on public blockchains like Ethereum.
differences.rightDesc: WASM powers web applications, serverless functions, game engines, and is increasingly used for secure, performant smart contracts on various platforms.
